A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All pages, equations, eleven figures, four tables, and Appendices A–G are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison despite reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original capacity simulations, MNIST and CIFAR-10 recall and classification experiments, baseline comparisons, and appendix robustness studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and experiments, including classification results in Table 1 and baseline recall results in Table 4.

M1.justification: The two-layer dynamics, threshold activation, reconstruction objective in Eq. (17), and learning procedure are unchanged. Asymmetric weights, heterogeneous thresholds, and sigmoid variants already appear in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic capacity and recall, MNIST, and CIFAR-10, including stored and unseen images. The represented tasks and perturbation scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains Krotov and Hopfield's Models A(i), A(ii), B, and C, including powers 5 and 10 for Model A. Table 1 also retains the original-image CNN comparison.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, network dimensions, classifier architectures, accuracy metrics, and parameter sweeps are unchanged. The added explicit Gaussian-noise specification documents an existing setup; it does not establish a changed experimental procedure.

E4.justification: Figures 1 and 6–11 retain the same threshold/noise sensitivity, neuron-ratio, insufficient-hidden-unit, asymmetric-weight, heterogeneous-threshold, sigmoid, and time-constant analyses. The revised mathematical noise argument is assessed under T1.

E5.justification: The plotted error bars are unchanged, and no run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised. Changes to theoretical noise variances do not change empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Unique minima remain 57,913 for MNIST and 49,982 for CIFAR-10. Table 1 retains hidden/visible/original accuracies of 95%/98%/99% and 40%/56%/88%, respectively. Table 4 and all plotted results also match. Appendix G's added fourfold time-scale statement describes an existing Figure 11 result.

T1.justification: The finite-size capacity argument is substantively revised. Section 2.1 and Appendix A.1 correct diagonal fluctuation variance from 1 to 2 and propagate this into the noise variance. Appendix D replaces v1's no-flip probability equality with a worst-case lower bound and a Gaussian-tail derivation. The bit-flip threshold condition is also corrected. These revise the mathematical justification, while retaining the asymptotic capacity and stability conclusions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: exponential capacity in hidden-unit count, distributed compositional representations, robust recall, biological plausibility, and generalization to unseen inputs.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 removes v1's suggestion that roughly ten times as many visible neurons suffices even away from the optimal threshold, replacing it with discussion of the threshold-specific bound. Section 3.2 moderates its characterization of CIFAR-10 accuracy, and Appendix G explicitly highlights the fourfold time-scale separation already illustrated.

D1.justification: Section 2.2 now explicitly specifies independent, zero-mean Gaussian visible-input perturbations in Eq. (13); v1 specified additive noise and its variance without stating that distribution. Other implementation details, including Xavier initialization, sigmoid-based optimization, and classifier architectures, are retained.

R1.justification: The same 29 cited works and substantive relationships to prior research are retained. Author-year citations, alphabetical references, and expanded author lists change bibliographic presentation rather than research positioning.

P1.justification: There are local prose and terminology edits, author/contact and acknowledgment updates, and expanded explanations in the retitled Appendix D. Citation presentation changes throughout, but the overall narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The manuscript adopts the ICLR conference layout throughout, changing page geometry, typography, title/author arrangement, headings, and running headers. Figures and tables are resized and redistributed: Figures 2–3 now share a page, and Figure 10 joins its Appendix F discussion. The underlying graphical and tabular content is retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting the diagonal fluctuation variance and expanding the finite-size probability derivation improve mathematical accuracy and transparency in Section 2.1 and Appendices A.1 and D. Removing the broad ten-to-one sufficiency statement also makes applicability more carefully stated. These are bounded improvements: the model, empirical evidence, and headline conclusions remain unchanged.
